children: Bernstein estimates that the nationwide FAA ground stop and the weekend recovery that followed cost American Airlines
about $345M pretax combined. By carrier, the Bernstein analyst team set a rough estimate of $113M for American
or $0.13 per share, $96M for Delta or $0.11 per share, $96M for United or $0.22 per share, and $40M for Southwest or $0.06 per share. American
was noted to have taken the largest dollar hit because it canceled the largest share of its schedule over the weekend.

When the airline causes a cancellation, it pays compensation in cash, miles, hotels, and meals on top of refunding the ticket. For the weekend flight disruption, since the cause was the FAA failure, carriers will refund passengers who choose not to travel but are not required to pay compensation or cover hotel and meal expenses.
The nationwide ground stop was only the third in U.S. history and the second longest after September 11, 2001.

title: American is expected to take the biggest hit from the weekend FAA disruption
